summary: The study describes a low-temperature atomic layer deposition (ALD) process for depositing ruthenium and ruthenium oxide using bis(2,4-dimethylpentadienyl)ruthenium and oxygen as precursors. The process is influenced by oxygen exposure time and pressure, with higher oxygen pressures promoting nucleation and growth of ruthenium films. The study highlights the ability to control the composition of the deposited films from metallic ruthenium to ruthenium oxide by adjusting oxygen exposure conditions. The process is characterized by a self-limiting reaction and is suitable for applications requiring conformal films on high-aspect-ratio structures.
evidence: We have studied the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of ruthenium using bis(2,4-dimethylpentadienyl) ruthenium and oxygen. We show that the process is achievable at a low operating temperature of 185 /C14 C. Variation in the exposure time and pressure of the oxygen counterreactant has significant effects on the nucleation, growth rate and composition of the deposited ruthenium films. High oxygen pressure helps to promote the nucleation of ruthenium on a silicon dioxide substrate. Although saturation conditions are achieved with the Ru precursor, saturation of the ruthenium growth rate with oxygen exposure is observed only for a small range of oxygen exposure. Increasing the oxygen exposure further results in the incorporation of oxygen in the deposited film to form ruthenium oxide, a process which is enhanced at higher deposition temperature.
